scores.name: graph-first
scores.notes: Every v1 file:line in its appendix resolves at 6cf05f5 (decay.py:21,34-35,48-69,66-67,91,100; api.py:328,379,401,414,420,439,453; ecs.py:212-213,222,295; consolidation.py:54-55,111-112; attention_log.py:64-65,108,129; durability.py:83,125; usd_target.py:47-48,101,102,225; ARCHITECTURE.md §7 step 3 = line 146, §15.2). Five typed graphs with nodes/edges/invariants/checks/sabotages, and it is the only draft that (a) splits resolution into values-by-strength vs authorization-by-intersection (v5 I5), which is what makes C3 non-trivial since LIVRPS cannot compute intersection; (b) notices that a per-event hash chain breaks on erase and proposes payload commitment by digest; (c) surfaces the E1-vs-ARCHITECTURE.md §7 lock collision inside G3 and the possible fourth-decay-eval-point collision with lock 2; (d) names the gen-stamp misattribution honestly against api.py:420. Tag pattern [A] (v6: V) is the cleanest of the three. Slips: 'five steps' lists four; stronger_than omits const/rules; mile 0 kill omits E4 and credits E2 with killing 'the line' (v6 §14 ties the line to E4); the LanceDB sentence is false against pyproject.toml:37 and vector_index.py:35-44.

scores.name: rust-seam-first
scores.notes: Deepest D1 work by a wide margin: per-seam signature, oracle, conformance check, numeric gate, crate; guarantees G1-G10; contract E; V-EVAL3 for the three-eval-point lock; O13/O14. Its v1 evidence is the best-mined of the three and all verified: ties fall to dict insertion order + stable sort (vector_index.py:155,167; api.py:415); query reads time.time() (api.py:399); attention entries carry no gen (attention_log.py:73); batch sum-then-clamp (ecs.py:211-212); two score paths (api.py:414 clamped, ecs.py:295 unclamped); v6's 1209600 s example is outside decay.py:34-35. Ruling B citation is ARCHITECTURE.md:50 under §2.1, correct. Structural gap: Proposed/Requested 'live in shadow records, not as govern events', so two lifecycle states are off the timeline, the S2 walker cannot see them, and V-REPLAY has no journaled verdict to reproduce; Expired has no exit edge. Contract E (order compared only above delta) contradicts V-REF-EQ/V-SCAN-EQ 'identical top-k'. ID collisions: G1-G10 are guarantees here but graphs in the task; S1-S4 are both seams and rules. Tags: repeatedly writes [V, v6 toy] / [V, v6 §6 on the toy; not re-run] / [V, decision D1 per v6] on J1, L2, L3, P3, T4 and the S1 row, against its own legend ('[V] about code means v1 source read at 6cf05f5') and against the task's instruction that anything not on this machine is [A]. The mile-3 package is not in the repo (confirmed: docs/v7 holds only RULINGS, inputs, jev, brief).

scores.name: mile-0-first

Its central move is correct and the others miss it: CLAUDE.md lists atomicity (E1) and the concurrency primitive (E3) under 'Locked decisions - do not re-open', so mile 0 is a MONETA.md §9 Round 4 escalation, not a merge; the E -> locked clause -> v1 line table is exactly what the Architect needs for the brief. Running the Python-only experiment in parallel with the round is sound (v6 §12 line 417: no Moneta changes). Kills named for both E2 and E4 (v6 §14). Expired state with signed exits is the best lifecycle drawing. Defects: the gen edge is defined as 'the generation live when the results it answers were served', which the substrate cannot know because signal_attention(weights) carries no echo (api.py:420) and the draft's own X3 keeps that signature; G1-4 (restores byte-equality) is mapped to V-UNDO, which tests probe answers not spec bytes; V-WRITE says the tuning pass appends govern{promote} when live, but promote is owner-signed under R4b; store layout has a trust/ directory while the text says trust is journaled state; renumbering miles reinterprets the RULED 'shadow-only through mile 4' without owner sign-off. Tags: honest re-assignment and explicit 'false in v1 [V, api.py:399-401]', but still uses the [V] glyph for 'on the v6 toy per v6 §8' rows that it admits were not checked here; X3's [V, api.py:453-458 precedent] verifies a precedent, not the rule.

Declare the fold step order before any V-ORACLE-FOLD / V-FOLD-EQ claim.

graph-first G4 diagram: the 'superseded (unsigned) -> Withdrawn' transition is not listed as a G1 event kind or govern.why, so under its own principle 6 ('if it isn't an edge, it isn't enforced') Withdrawn is unenforced. Either add a journaled withdraw/supersede event or define Withdrawn as derived from the next propose.

A near-tie pair straddling the k boundary can legitimately flip under contract E. Restate the pass condition as 'identical except for pairs within delta, which must be ordered by the total order'.

scores.name: graph-first
scores.notes: Strongest graph model. It has five typed graphs, an edge table, and invariant-to-check-to-sabotage rows. It is the only draft that separates value resolution (by strength) from authorization resolution (by intersection) and adds V-NARROW. It is also the only one that notices a per-event hash chain breaks under erase, and it answers with payload commitment by digest plus re-genesis for compact. It surfaces the E1 lock collision inside G3 rather than hiding it, and admits the gen stamp is applied at append time because signal_attention takes no echo (api.py:420, verified). Tag discipline is good: toy and v5 claims are written '[A] (v6: V)', and every v1 [V] I spot-checked matches (decay.py:48-69 and :66-67, consolidation.py:54-55 and :111-112, usd_target.py:101/102/225, attention_log.py:64-65, ARCHITECTURE §7). Weaknesses: (1) G2-7 says the USD resolver reproduces Resolved(c,n) 'for every stack', but LIVRPS can't compute intersection, so the claim can't hold for authorization fields. (2) The stronger_than order leaves out the const and rules tiers. (3) Nothing invalidates a checkpoint sealed while g was Promoted once g rolls back, so V-HASHGATE would accept a stale checkpoint whose hash is valid. (4) 'Open takes five steps' lists four. (5) Rule ID D1 collides with decision D1. (6) erase and revector are added to the signed set beyond R5; they are tagged [P], but this is scope growth on a ruled item.

scores.name: rust-seam-first
scores.notes: Deepest Rust engineering. Each seam gets a signature, oracle, conformance check, numeric gate and crate. §3.7 lists what the rest of v7 must guarantee for the seams to stay pure: a total-order tie key, canonical bytes, time passed in as an argument, and a gen edge on attention. It catches several real v1 hazards I verified: ties fall to dict order plus a stable sort (vector_index.py:155-167, api.py:415); ecs.py:295 does not clamp cosine while api.py:414 does; v1 sums a batch then clamps once (ecs.py:211-212); and v6's 14-day example is outside v1's 60 s to 24 h bounds (decay.py:34-35). Graph-side contributions: O13 (signed-set events stay inert until their sig lands, tracked by signed_through_seq), O14 (rollback reseals, and V-CKPT's sabotage is opening from a pre-rollback checkpoint), and V-EVAL3 for the three-evaluation-point lock. Weaknesses: (1) Contract E (a δ-ulp tolerance), together with O5 saying no shared exp is needed between oracle and Rust, weakens D1's 'exact Python oracle'. (2) Tags break its own rule: S4 and rule S4 are '[V, decision D1 per v6]', and J1/P3/T4/L2/L3 are '[V, v6 toy]', although the toy isn't on this machine and these should be [A]. (3) Proposed and Requested live in unjournaled 'shadow records' that aren't in the store layout, so V-SHADOW and V-REPLAY can't be checked from the journal. (4) Nothing on authorization narrowing. (5) Nothing on erase under the hash chain. (6) Invariant IDs collide heavily with rule IDs (J1-J7 against J1-J10, L1-L7 against L1-L3, P, D, and G1-G10 guarantees against G1-G2 rules), which hurts traceability.

scores.name: mile-0-first
scores.notes: Most honest about v1 reality. A §2 table, all lines verified, shows main is the opposite of v7's assumptions on five points: reads write (api.py:401), the vector index is authoritative (ARCHITECTURE.md:146), the attention log depends on the GIL, prune deletes (consolidation.py:167-169), and the WAL is unlinked (durability.py:125). It correctly reframes mile 0 as a MONETA.md §9 Round 4 escalation with a table of each overturned lock, which matches CLAUDE.md. It runs the cheap experiment in parallel so its report can feed the round, and it gives every check a mile column. Rust sequencing is clean: Python oracles first, Rust in a single later mile. Weaknesses: (1) It renumbers miles, then reinterprets R4's ruled 'shadow-only through mile 4' as through v7 mile 5 (and G4-5 says 'until mile 6'), and moves R2's 'mile 2 β arm' to mile 1. It flags this, but it is reinterpreting the text of a ruling. (2) The `gen` edge is defined as 'the generation live when the results it answers were served'. That can't be computed under the locked signal_attention(weights) signature (api.py:420), and both other drafts state this. (3) G4-2 says every edge is a signed govern, but the diagram has an unsigned propose and an unsigned ceiling→Expired edge. (4) V-WRITE lets a tuning pass append govern{why: promote} 'when live', which contradicts owner-signed promote (R4b). (5) Nothing on erase versus the hash chain, authorization narrowing, or checkpoint staleness after rollback. (6) It adds a second approval to 'the one ask'.

graft_from_others: From rust-seam-first §3.7: the guarantees that keep the seams pure. Bring them in as G1/G3 invariants with checks: the total-order tie key (score desc, seq asc, record_id asc) plus V-TIES; canonical event bytes, with V-CHAIN's sabotage being 'hash over a re-serialised object'; and time passed in as an argument, never read inside a seam (api.py:399 reads time.time()).

From rust-seam-first: O13. Signed-set events stay inert until signed, a Verdict reports signed_through_seq, and V-SIGSET's sabotage becomes 'an unsigned adopt acted on'. This settles inline versus separate signatures when the key is off-machine.

From rust-seam-first: O14. A rollback reseals over a rebuilt checkpoint, and V-CKPT (or graph-first's V-HASHGATE) gains the sabotage 'open from a pre-rollback checkpoint'. This closes graph-first's stale-checkpoint gap under G4-5.

From rust-seam-first: V-EVAL3, which states that the recall fold is a pure view that writes nothing under the three-evaluation-point lock (ARCHITECTURE.md:84-90). It turns graph-first's O2 question into a check.

From rust-seam-first: C8 / V-BOUNDS with the sabotage 'v1 DecayConfig bounds used for recall λ'. Recall-half-life bounds must be decoupled from decay.py:34-35, because v6's 14-day example is out of range.

From rust-seam-first: the oracle hazards. The per-batch versus per-event clamp (ecs.py:211-212) must be declared before V-ORACLE-FOLD means anything. The scan oracle is api.query's clamped path, not ecs.py:295.

From rust-seam-first: the S2 mutation corpus (every byte flip, deletion, truncation, adjacent swap and signature retarget), V-IMPORTS, trust-store pins as journaled govern{const} content, and a §9 locks table.

From mile-0-first: the §2 'what main actually is' table, and framing mile 0 explicitly as a MONETA.md §9 Round 4 escalation, with each overturned lock and its v1 line (E1 to ARCHITECTURE.md:146/152, E3 to §5.1, E4 to consolidation.py:167-169).

From mile-0-first: run the Python-only experiment alongside the escalation so its report becomes evidence for the round. Keep v6/RULINGS mile numbering, though, so R2's and R4's ruled mile references stay literal.

From mile-0-first: a per-check 'mile' column in the checks table, V-LEAK (eval sets after a rollback contain no tagged attention), and attack 4 on how an indefinite Expired/Overdue hold interacts with the §15.2 rotation at 50k prims.
defects_to_fix: graph-first §2 G2 'Two resolution rules' against G2-7/D5/V-C3: it claims the plain and USD resolvers agree on Resolved(c,n) 'for every stack', but USD's LIVRPS only does strength resolution and can't compute the intersection used for scopes and exclusions. Either restrict C3 to value fields, or state how USD represents narrowing. Until then the claim can't be proven.

graph-first §2 G2 stronger_than: the order lists owner@c > … > owner@root > self, but the tiers include const and rules. Their place in the order, and whether rules enters read-time resolution at all, isn't stated, so V-OWNER can't check against a complete order.

graph-first G3-3/V-HASHGATE with G4-5: nothing invalidates a fold checkpoint sealed while g was Promoted once g rolls back. The checkpoint's hash still matches, so a stale retention fold that includes g's attention is loaded. Add a reseal on rollback and a sabotage for opening a pre-rollback checkpoint.
graph-first §3 'Open': says 'five steps' but lists four.
graph-first §4: rule ID 'D1' (purity) collides with decision D1 (the Rust seam rule). Rename it.
graph-first G1 table: marking erase and revector as signed extends R5's ruled signed set. It is tagged [P] but should be raised as an open decision against R5, not added silently.

rust-seam-first C4/G5/O5 (Contract E): a δ-ulp tolerance, plus 'needs no shared exp between the Python oracle and Rust', weakens D1's 'exact Python oracle'. Make bit-exactness with a pure-Python port of the shared exp the default, and keep the tolerance only as a measured, recorded fallback.

rust-seam-first tags: S4 and rule S4 are '[V, decision D1 per v6]'; §3.2's '[V, v6 §6 on the toy; not re-run]'; and T4/P3/J1/L2/L3 are '[V, v6 toy]'. The toy and v6's decisions aren't verified on this machine, which breaks the draft's own rule that what can't be checked here is [A].

rust-seam-first §4.4/§5: Proposed and Requested live in 'shadow records' that aren't journaled and aren't in the store layout. V-SHADOW, V-REPLAY and V-ONEPENDING then have no journal-derivable state to check.
rust-seam-first: no erase design under the per-event running hash. Deleting payload bytes in place breaks every later h_n, so V-CHAIN and erasure conflict. Graph-first's payload commitment is needed.
rust-seam-first §4.2: no authorization-narrowing invariant, so scopes resolved by strength would let a child widen its parent and no check catches it. V-NARROW is missing.
rust-seam-first: invariant IDs (J1-J7, P1-P6, D1-D6, L1-L7, G1-G10) collide with rule IDs (J1-J10, P1-P5, L1-L3, G1-G2) and with decision D1. Cross-references like 'V-HOLD | J7, L2' are ambiguous.

mile-0-first §9 and G4-5: renumbering the miles and then reading R4's ruled 'shadow-only through mile 4' as 'through v7 mile 5' (and 'until mile 6' in G4-5) reinterprets a RULED item. The β arm also moves from R2's 'mile 2' to mile 1. Keep RULINGS numbering, or escalate the renumbering to the owner.

mile-0-first G1 `gen` edge: defined as the generation 'live when the results it answers were served'. That can't be computed without an echo, and signal_attention(weights) is a locked signature (api.py:420). It has to be the generation live at append, with the misattribution window stated.
mile-0-first G4-2: 'each [edge] is a signed govern' contradicts its own diagram, which has an unsigned propose and an unsigned ceiling→Expired transition.
mile-0-first V-WRITE: 'a tuning pass appends … govern{why: promote} when live' contradicts R4(b). Promote is owner-signed, and the tuner or tuning pass can't sign. It should append only propose.
mile-0-first: no handling of erase versus the hash chain, authorization narrowing, or checkpoint staleness after rollback.

All three: none enforces with a check that the retention fold excludes rolled-back attention from attended_count (consolidation.py:111-112 reads attended_count, incremented at ecs.py:213) and not only from utility. V-UNDO's sabotage should name attended_count explicitly.
